prompt: Split an arithmetic expression into tokens while KEEPING the operators, using zero-width lookahead and lookbehind so the split happens beside a delimiter instead of consuming it.
explanation: Lookahead (?=...) and lookbehind (?<=...) match a position rather than characters, so split cuts the string without removing anything. Using both alternatives means every operator gets a cut on each side and ends up alone between two cuts. Because a cut before a leading operator opens an empty first piece -- and split only trims empty pieces from the end -- the filtering step is what makes "-5+3" come out with four tokens instead of five.
hints: The split pattern is two zero-width alternatives joined by |: one lookbehind and one lookahead over the same operator character class.
Put '-' first inside the character class, as in [-+/*], so it is read as a literal and not as a range.
split can hand back an empty first element; copy only the non-empty pieces into the list.
